channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan is a driving force in the Organization of Turkic States, says Secretary General
item.description: The Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States, Kubanychbek Omuraliev, congratulated Uzbekistan on its 35th Independence Day. He highlighted Uzbekistan's significant contributions to the Turkic world's unity through initiatives in transport, trade, digital transformation, education, culture, and regional dialogue. Omuraliev noted Uzbekistan's impressive reforms under President Shavkat Mirziyoyev over the past decade.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev congratulates Mirziyoyev on Uzbekistan's 35th Independence Day at SCO Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on their countries' 35th Independence Days during the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan. Tokayev thanked Kyrgyzstan for its hospitality and praised the SCO's growth into a major international organization over 25 years, emphasizing mutual trust and respect for sovereignty.

item.title: Uzbekistan President holds dialogue on improving business conditions
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with entrepreneurs in Khiva to discuss improving conditions for businesses. The focus shifted from supporting startups to fostering growth for existing enterprises, emphasizing access to finance, technology, markets, and a predictable regulatory environment. Business credit portfolios have nearly tripled.

item.title: Four Uzbek citizens arrested in South Korea for financing terrorism
item.description: Four Uzbek citizens have been arrested in South Korea on suspicion of financing terrorism. They are accused of sending cryptocurrency and vehicles to the "Tavhid va Jihod Katibasi" group in Syria. The main suspect allegedly purchased and sent 11 used cars and two excavators from South Korea.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement new poverty reduction and employment system
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a new system for poverty reduction and increasing employment. Regional and district headquarters will receive additional powers and resources totaling 3.2 trillion soums. Governors and economic officials will dedicate three days a week to poverty and employment issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces new system for poverty reduction and employment
item.description: Uzbekistan is launching a completely new system for poverty reduction and income growth, announced President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Districts will receive 3.2 trillion soums in resources. Governors and economic officials will focus on poverty and employment issues three days a week. This approach was developed after studying poverty in the Khorezm region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan faces climate crisis with melting glaciers and billions in damages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has submitted a draft National Adaptation Plan through 2035, calling for a major overhaul of its climate risk management system. Rising temperatures have caused glaciers to shrink by 16-17% since 2000, increasing flood risks and impacting water supplies, agriculture, and hydropower.

item.title: Uzbekistan Engages in High-Level Diplomatic Meetings with India, Azerbaijan, and Pakistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's foreign policy prioritizes trust and cooperation. Prime Minister Modi visited Uzbekistan for talks with President Mirziyoyev on August 29-30, focusing on trade, energy, and healthcare. Meetings also occurred between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and Uzbekistan and Pakistan, discussing economic and regional issues.

item.title: Tajikistan Promotes Military Officers to General Ranks
item.description: Several Tajik military officials have been promoted to general ranks, with some receiving the rank for the first time. The promotions span various leadership positions within the security forces.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders Poverty Reduction for 230,000 Families by End of 2026
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed to lift 230,000 families out of poverty by the end of 2026. Regional and district authorities are tasked with effectively organizing employment initiatives to place 350,000 people in permanent jobs and increase incomes for one million citizens.

item.title: Climate Change May Worsen Poverty in Kyrgyzstan, National Plan Warns
item.description: Climate change in Kyrgyzstan disproportionately affects vulnerable populations, including women, children, youth, the elderly, people with disabilities, and low-income families. Over 57% of the population lives in rural areas dependent on agriculture, making them susceptible to droughts, water shortages, and land degradation. The plan highlights increased burdens on women due to resource scarcity and caregiving responsibilities.

item.title: Bishkek and Osh to Enhance Climate Resilience in National Adaptation Plan
item.description: Bishkek and Osh are identified as climate-vulnerable cities in Kyrgyzstan's National Adaptation Plan through 2035. Measures will address heat stress, utility network strain, and infrastructure risks from heavy precipitation. Plans include reviewing urban planning documents, ensuring business continuity for critical facilities, and increasing green spaces and water drainage solutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan highlights healthcare worker safety concerns at Mongolian conference
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Healthcare Workers' Trade Union chairman addressed an international conference in Mongolia, emphasizing rising threats to healthcare workers. He noted that aggression, physical violence, and lack of legal protection are now significant risks, alongside traditional occupational hazards. Stricter penalties and preventive measures are needed to ensure worker safety.

item.title: Uzbekistan revises social registry, extends child benefits for working mothers
item.description: Uzbekistan will now provide benefits to working mothers until their child turns one year old. The social registry system for needy populations is being revised. Families registered will receive vouchers to cover childcare, educational centers, transportation, and dormitory expenses at higher education institutions.

item.title: Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon awards state honors to security personnel
item.description: On September 3, 2026, Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon presented state awards and special ranks to representatives of law enforcement, judicial, and military structures. The ceremony, held in honor of the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence, recognized their role in safeguarding national security and stability.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Conduct Nationwide Business Census from October 15 to November 30, 2026
item.description: Uzbekistan will conduct a large-scale census of business entities from October 15 to November 30, 2026, to update information on enterprises and organizations. The census aims to inventory active economic units and address the significant shadow economy, estimated at 23% of the country's GDP.

item.title: OPEC Fund to lend Tajikistan $30 million for road reconstruction in GBAO
item.description: Tajikistan and the OPEC Fund for International Development have signed their first Partnership Strategy for 2026-2028. The initial project involves reconstructing the Rushon-Vardz road in Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region, with the OPEC Fund providing a $30 million loan for the first phase. This will upgrade 82.2 km of the Dushanbe-Kulma-China highway.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces new system for poverty reduction and employment, mayors to focus on these issues three days a week
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing a completely new system for combating poverty and addressing employment issues. Local government heads (mayors) will now dedicate three days per week to these matters. This initiative aims to improve the socio-economic conditions of citizens.

item.title: Uzbek President criticizes ineffective use of funds allocated for poverty reduction
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized the insufficient effectiveness of credit resources used for poverty reduction and income growth. He noted that while 314 trillion soums were allocated for entrepreneurship projects in the past three years, the impact on poverty reduction varies significantly across districts.

item.title: Uzbek President Criticizes Regional Leaders for Inability to Create Jobs
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev criticized regional leaders for lacking the knowledge or will to create employment. He noted that 62,000 individuals who received bank loans for businesses are struggling to repay them, indicating a lack of effectiveness in loan resource utilization.

item.title: Number of Needy People in Uzbekistan Decreased to 1.5 Million
item.description: The number of needy citizens in Uzbekistan has decreased to 1.5 million. However, the president criticized district and mahalla officials for their hesitation and unwillingness to take responsibility for poverty and unemployment issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank to Strengthen Oversight of Bank Currency Risks and Asset Quality
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank is tightening requirements for banks on reserves and currency risk management, while transitioning financial reporting to international standards. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov stated that the regulator is shifting focus from identifying future risks to enhancing the overall stability of the financial system.

item.title: SCO Countries to Conduct Joint Drills for Emergency Situations
item.description: Following a summit in Bishkek, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states agreed to provide aid to countries affected by emergencies. Kyrgyzstan proposed a mechanism for this, while Russia suggested resource reserve funds. SCO nations will prioritize humanitarian assistance to members facing natural or man-made disasters.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Begins Construction of Infectious Disease Research Center
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new scientific center for infectious disease research in Kyrgyzstan, according to the Ministry of Health. The facility aims to conduct laboratory research, scientific work, and train specialists to enhance the country's response to disease threats.

item.title: New judge appointed to Moskovsky District Court in Chui region
item.description: Artur Shadybekov has been appointed judge of the Moskovsky District Court of Chui region for a five-year term. He took the oath of office and officially assumed his duties following presidential decrees. Supreme Court Chairman Mederbek Satyev attended the ceremony.

item.title: Uzbekistan aims to attract more family tourists from India with new flights
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase tourist flow from India, focusing on family travel with children. Discussions are underway with Indian bloggers and influencers to promote Uzbekistan as a safe destination. New Hyderabad-Tashkent flights will launch on September 28, operating twice weekly.

item.title: Kyrgyz poet Akbar Ryskulov explains signing of 'letter of 75'
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's People's Poet and diplomat Akbar Ryskulov testified in court regarding the 'letter of 75'. He stated he signed the appeal for early presidential elections because he believed it aimed to develop the economy and ensure stability, seeing no ulterior motive.

item.title: Indian citizens can now enter Uzbekistan visa-free with valid visas from 8 countries
item.description: Starting September 1, 2026, Indian citizens with valid multiple-entry business or tourist visas from eight specific countries or Schengen states can enter Uzbekistan visa-free for up to 30 days. A return flight ticket is also required.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea's LS Corporation Discuss Energy Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with representatives from South Korea's LS Corporation to discuss bilateral cooperation in the energy sector. The meeting focused on attracting investments and implementing joint projects, with Tajikistan presenting its energy sector investment opportunities.

item.title: Nearly 1 million hectares of unrecorded land clarified in Uzbekistan
item.description: As a result of the agricultural census, the boundaries and categories of 985,500 hectares of land, previously not reflected in records, have been clarified in Uzbekistan. Permanent statistical registers for agriculture will be formed.

item.title: Tajikistan and EU Discuss Industrial Cooperation, Focusing on Light Industry and Cotton Processing
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry met with the EU Ambassador to discuss industrial cooperation. Key areas included light industry development, textile production, and cotton processing. Both sides expressed readiness for continued dialogue and mutually beneficial collaboration.

item.title: Denmark Deploys Troops to Greenland Amidst Rising Tensions with US and Geopolitical Instability
item.description: Denmark has sent conscripted soldiers to Greenland for the first time in recent history, aiming to strengthen its Arctic position amid diplomatic friction with the US and regional geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Tashkent agency vows to prevent demolition of historic house on Bobur Street
item.description: Tashkent's Cultural Heritage Agency will prevent any illegal attempts to demolish or alter the historic house at 7 Bobur Street. The agency stated the building's status as a cultural heritage site will be maintained, and previous proposals to remove it from the national register were rejected.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's AI-92 gasoline prices increased by nearly 1.5 percent in August
item.description: In August, AI-92 gasoline prices in Kyrgyzstan rose by 1.46 percent, reaching 89.11 soms per liter. AI-95 gasoline saw a 0.53 percent increase, costing 109.27 soms. Diesel fuel prices slightly decreased by 0.17 percent to 101.69 soms. Since the start of the year, gasoline prices have increased significantly.

item.title: Chingiz Kaziev appointed Deputy Chief of Staff of Kyrgyzstan's Parliament
item.description: Chingiz Kaziev has been appointed Deputy Chief of Staff of the Zhogorku Kenesh, Kyrgyzstan's parliament. Venera Kulataeva, the former Deputy Chief of Staff, is now the First Deputy Chief of Staff. These appointments were formalized by Marlen Mamataliev, the Speaker of the Zhogorku Kenesh.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran discuss cooperation prospects for Sangtudinskaya HPP-2
item.description: On September 2, 2026, Dushanbe hosted a meeting between Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources and the CEO of Iran's "Sangob" company. They discussed the current state and future prospects of cooperation in the energy sector, specifically regarding the Sangtudinskaya HPP-2.

item.title: Air Arabia Selected to Transport Kyrgyz Pilgrims to Hajj in 2027
item.description: Air Arabia has been chosen to transport 6,060 Kyrgyz pilgrims to Saudi Arabia for Hajj in 2027. The decision followed a competition by an interdepartmental commission. In previous years, Kyrgyz pilgrims were transported by Saudi Arabian airlines Flyadeal and Jazeera Airways.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Egypt for State Visit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Cairo for a state visit to Egypt at the invitation of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi. Xi Jinping was warmly welcomed by President el-Sisi and his wife. The Chinese president highlighted the long-standing friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation between China and Egypt.

item.title: Tashkent traffic volume increased by 30% on the first day of the academic year
item.description: Tashkent experienced a 30% increase in car traffic on the first day of the academic year. Most major intersections are connected to a digital system that monitors road conditions, traffic light operation, vehicle queues, and public transport movement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Integrates into Global Market Through Economic Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan has transitioned from a closed, resource-based economy to a modern model integrating into the global market. Reforms like currency convertibility and tax liberalization have attracted foreign investment, particularly in green energy, textiles, and pharmaceuticals. Trade now spans over 160 countries, with key partners including China, Russia, Turkey, South Korea, and Central Asian nations.
